patients.summary: Retired construction supervisor and former heavy smoker who joined in 2022 with treated hypertension. Screening found a stage I lung adenocarcinoma (lobectomy 2023), then a testicular germ cell tumor treated with BEP that left bleomycin pulmonary fibrosis and cisplatin-related CKD 3b, then a clear cell renal cancer that has spread to the lungs; he is on a treatment break and thinking about his goals.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Mr. Marino called about joining. His previous doctor retired last year and he has been getting refills through an urgent care. Explained membership and that he keeps his insurance for labs and specialists. Booked new patient visit 5/10 at 8:40. Release signed over the phone for records from the prior office, faxed today.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
38 pages received by fax from the patient's previous internal medicine office, covering 2014 to 2021. Summary for the chart:
- Hypertension, on lisinopril 5 mg daily for several years, last office BP 134/82.
- Allergies: IV contrast (hives), sulfa antibiotics (rash).
- Screening colonoscopy 2019: normal, repeat in 10 years.
- Tobacco: current smoker, counseled at several visits.
Scanned under Media. Flagged for the new patient visit.

orders.order: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
61 y/o man establishing care. Prior PCP retired; records from that office reviewed.

HTN for about ten years, on lisinopril 5 mg daily, no side effects. Doesn't check BP at home. No chest pain, no breathing complaints beyond the usual morning smoker's throat clearing, no leg swelling.

Tobacco: about a pack a day since his late teens, roughly 40 pack-years. Has tried to quit twice, longest about four months. Says he is "thinking about it seriously" now that he is retired and his wife is after him about it.
Alcohol: a beer or two on weekends. No other substances.
Retired from construction (site supervisor, commercial jobs). Married, lives with his wife.

PMH: hypertension. PSH: none.
FH: father died of lung cancer at 67. Paternal uncle had kidney cancer in his 70s. Mother, 83, has high blood pressure.
Allergies: IV contrast dye - hives. Sulfa antibiotics - rash.
Meds: lisinopril 5 mg daily.
Prevention: colonoscopy 2019 normal per old records. No pneumonia or shingles vaccines on file; last tetanus unknown.

Exam: BP 136/84. Well-appearing, smells of smoke. Lungs clear, no wheeze, normal effort. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema. Skin fine.

A/P
1. HTN - near goal on lisinopril 5, continue. CMP, UA.
2. Tobacco use, 40 pack-years - spent a good while on this. He wants to try cold turkey first; we talked about patch and medicines if that fails and he'll let me know. Qualifies for annual lung cancer screening; low-dose CT ordered, explained what it can find and the chance of a false alarm.
3. Health maintenance: CBC, lipids, A1c, hep C and HIV screen today. PCV20, Tdap and first Shingrix given. Shingrix #2 in 2-6 months. Colonoscopy due 2029.
RTC 6 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Andrew, your labs from Tuesday look good. Kidney function, blood counts, sugar and cholesterol are all fine, and the hepatitis C and HIV screens are negative. The CT scheduler should call you this week. Let me know how the quitting is going.

documents.title: Smoking
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Doc - figured you'd want to know I've been off cigarettes since the 1st. Nine days. Chewing a lot of gum. Also never heard from anyone about that CT scan, can you check on it?

documents.title: RE: Smoking
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That is great news, Andrew. The first few weeks are the hardest, and if cravings get bad the patch is still an option, just tell me. I asked our staff to chase the CT; the order was there but the imaging center lost the referral. They will call you to schedule.

procedures.procedure: Immunization administration

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Second Shingrix given L deltoid, lot recorded. Tolerated. Pt reports 15 days smoke free. Low-dose CT scheduled for 9/6.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
Indication: Annual lung cancer screening, 40 pack-years, quit 08/2022.
Technique: Low-dose helical CT of the chest without contrast.
Comparison: None.
Findings: Solid nodule in the left upper lobe, apicoposterior segment, measuring 19 mm in mean diameter, with lobulated margins. No other pulmonary nodules. No consolidation or pleural effusion. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy by size. Heart size normal. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable.
Lung-RADS category: 4B.
reports.conclusion: 19 mm solid left upper lobe nodule, Lung-RADS 4B, suspicious. PET-CT and/or tissue sampling recommended.

documents.title: Low-dose CT result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt with the screening CT. 19 mm LUL nodule, Lung-RADS 4B. Told him plainly this needs to be worked up for cancer, and that if it is cancer, finding it this size is the reason we screen. He was quiet, asked good questions. Wife on speaker. PET-CT ordered and urgent pulmonology referral placed. Will call him when PET is back.

reports.text:
Indication: 19 mm left upper lobe nodule.
Technique: F-18 FDG PET with low-dose non-contrast CT for attenuation correction.
Findings: The left upper lobe nodule is FDG-avid, SUVmax 6.2. No FDG-avid mediastinal, hilar or supraclavicular lymph nodes. No other pulmonary uptake. No abnormal uptake in the liver, adrenals or skeleton. Physiologic activity elsewhere.
reports.conclusion: Hypermetabolic left upper lobe nodule (SUVmax 6.2) concerning for primary lung malignancy. No nodal or distant metastatic disease.

reports.text:
Specimen: Left upper lobe nodule, navigational bronchoscopic transbronchial biopsy and brushings.
Gross: Multiple tan tissue fragments, aggregate 0.6 cm.
Microscopic: Fragments of lung parenchyma infiltrated by malignant glandular epithelium with acinar architecture. Immunostains: TTF-1 positive, napsin A positive, p40 negative.
reports.conclusion: Adenocarcinoma of the lung (non-small cell carcinoma), left upper lobe.

documents.title: Pulmonology Consultation and Bronchoscopy
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Re: Andrew Marino, DOB 03/08/1961

Thank you for referring Mr. Marino, a 61-year-old former smoker (40 pack-years, quit 08/2022) with a 19 mm left upper lobe nodule found on screening low-dose CT. PET-CT showed avidity in the nodule (SUVmax 6.2) without nodal or distant uptake.

He has no cough, hemoptysis or weight loss. Exercise tolerance is good; he walks a mile with his wife most days.
Allergies: iodinated contrast (hives), sulfonamide antibiotics (rash).
Medications: lisinopril 5 mg daily.

Exam: SpO2 97% on room air. Lungs clear bilaterally. No lymphadenopathy.

Procedure 10/18: Navigational bronchoscopy with radial EBUS confirmation; transbronchial biopsies and brushings of the LUL lesion. Moderate sedation. No pneumothorax on post-procedure film. Tolerated well.

Pathology (final 10/21): adenocarcinoma, TTF-1 and napsin A positive.

Impression: Clinical stage I non-small cell lung cancer, left upper lobe adenocarcinoma. Spirometry in clinic adequate for lobectomy.
Plan: Referred to thoracic surgery for resection. I discussed the diagnosis with him and his wife today.

Pulmonary Medicine

documents.title: Thoracic Surgery Consultation
documents.author: thoracic surgery
documents.body:
Patient: Andrew Marino
Reason for consult: left upper lobe adenocarcinoma, clinical stage I

Mr. Marino is a 61-year-old retired construction supervisor referred by pulmonology after bronchoscopic biopsy confirmed adenocarcinoma in a 19 mm LUL nodule. PET staging negative for nodal or distant disease. He stopped smoking in August.

PMH: hypertension. No prior surgery.
Meds: lisinopril 5 mg daily.
Allergies: IV contrast (hives); sulfa antibiotics (rash).

Exam: Fit-appearing. Lungs clear. Heart regular.

Assessment: Clinical stage I NSCLC, LUL. Good functional status; spirometry acceptable.
Plan: Robotic-assisted left upper lobectomy with mediastinal lymph node dissection, scheduled for 01/10/2023. Pre-operative evaluation by his primary care physician requested. Risks, benefits and recovery discussed with him and his wife; consent signed.

Thoracic Surgery

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate 72. Normal axis. Normal intervals. No ST or T wave abnormality.
reports.conclusion: Normal ECG.

Electrocardiogram, 12-lead, with interpretation

documents.title: Pre-operative Evaluation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Pre-op eval for robotic L upper lobectomy 1/10/23 (thoracic surgery).

S: Feels well. Still not smoking, four months now, proud of it. Climbs two flights without stopping, no chest pain, no syncope, no orthopnea. No bleeding history. Never had anesthesia. No family anesthesia problems.
Meds: lisinopril 5 mg.
Allergies: contrast dye (hives), sulfa abx (rash).

O: BP and vitals as recorded. Lungs clear. Heart RRR, no murmur. No edema.
ECG: NSR, normal.

A/P: Intermediate-risk surgery, functional capacity >4 METs, no active cardiac conditions. RCRI 1 (intrathoracic surgery). OK to proceed from a medical standpoint.
- Hold lisinopril the morning of surgery, resume when eating and BP allows.
- BMP, CBC today.
- Contrast allergy flagged for the hospital.
Note faxed to thoracic surgery.

events.reason: left upper lobectomy for lung adenocarcinoma

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (650 mg) by mouth every 6 hours as needed for pain

reports.text:
Specimen A: Left upper lobe, lobectomy. Specimen B-F: Mediastinal and hilar lymph nodes, stations 5, 6, 7, 10L, 11L.
Tumor: Invasive adenocarcinoma, acinar predominant. Size 2.0 cm. Visceral pleural invasion not identified. Lymphovascular invasion not identified. Bronchial, vascular and parenchymal margins negative.
Lymph nodes: 0 of 9 involved.
Pathologic stage: pT1b N0.
reports.conclusion: Invasive adenocarcinoma, left upper lobe, 2.0 cm, margins negative, 0/9 nodes; pT1b N0, stage IA.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Thoracic Surgery
documents.author: thoracic surgery
documents.body:
Admit 01/10/2023  Discharge 01/13/2023
Procedure: Robotic-assisted left upper lobectomy with mediastinal lymph node dissection (01/10).
Diagnosis: Left upper lobe adenocarcinoma.

Hospital course: Uncomplicated. Chest tube removed POD 2 after air leak resolved. Ambulating independently, on room air, SpO2 94-96%. Pain controlled with acetaminophen.
Final pathology pending at discharge.
Allergies: iodinated contrast (urticaria), sulfonamide antibiotics (rash).

Discharge medications:
- Lisinopril 5 mg daily (resumed)
- Acetaminophen 650 mg every 6 hours as needed for pain
No NSAIDs for now.

Follow-up: thoracic surgery clinic 2 weeks; PCP within 1-2 weeks. Walk daily, no lifting over 10 lb for 4 weeks, no driving while sore.

conditions.label: History of stage I non-small cell lung cancer (status post left upper lobectomy)

procedures.procedure: Transitional care management, moderate complexity

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 11 days after robotic LUL lobectomy (1/10-1/13). Final path came through last week: 2.0 cm adenocarcinoma, margins clear, 0/9 nodes, pT1b N0 - stage IA. Thoracic surgery told him no chemo or radiation needed, surveillance CTs.

S: Sore along the left side when he twists, sleeping in the recliner a few nights. Using acetaminophen 650 two or three times a day, nothing stronger. Walking around the block twice daily. No fever, breathing about like before, no leg swelling. Not smoking.
Meds reconciled: lisinopril 5 daily, acetaminophen 650 q6h prn.

O: Incisions clean and dry, healing. Lungs: slightly diminished at left apex, otherwise clear. Heart regular. Calves soft.

A/P
1. Stage I NSCLC s/p LUL lobectomy - recovering well. Surveillance per thoracic surgery (CT ~6 months). Updated problem list.
2. Post-op pain - acetaminophen as needed is fine; avoid ibuprofen for now.
3. HTN - fine, continue lisinopril.
4. Former smoker - 6 months quit; reinforced.
RTC for annual physical in spring.

procedures.procedure: Preventive visit, established patient, 40-64

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam.

Interval: L upper lobectomy in January for stage IA adenocarcinoma, recovered. Side twinge with lifting now and then, takes acetaminophen maybe once a week. Back to walking 2 miles. Still smoke-free since last August.
ROS: no cough, no hemoptysis, no chest pain, no urinary symptoms, no weight loss.
Meds: lisinopril 5 mg daily; acetaminophen 650 mg prn.
Allergies: IV contrast, sulfa abx.
Social: retired, does odd jobs on the house, wife well.

Exam: BP as charted, near goal. Well. HEENT normal. Lungs clear, healed port sites left chest. Heart RRR. Abdomen benign. GU deferred by pt. Skin no concerning lesions. No edema.

A/P
- HTN: at goal, continue.
- Hx NSCLC: surveillance CT in July with thoracic surgery.
- Labs: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c.
- Vaccines: PCV20, Tdap, Shingrix done 2022. Flu and COVID in October.
- Colonoscopy next 2029.
One year, or sooner.

reports.text:
Indication: Surveillance, s/p left upper lobectomy 01/2023 for adenocarcinoma.
Technique: Helical CT of the chest without IV contrast (contrast allergy).
Comparison: PET-CT 09/27/2022.
Findings: Postsurgical changes of left upper lobectomy with staple line intact. Expected volume loss on the left. No new or enlarging pulmonary nodules. No pleural effusion. No adenopathy within the limits of a non-contrast study. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Expected post-lobectomy changes. No evidence of recurrence.

documents.title: Thoracic Surgery Follow-up
documents.author: thoracic surgery
documents.body:
Mr. Marino returns 6 months after robotic left upper lobectomy for pT1b N0 adenocarcinoma. Feels well, active, no cough, no chest wall pain at rest. Remains off cigarettes.
CT chest 7/11 without contrast: postsurgical changes only, no recurrence.
Exam: incisions well healed, lungs clear.
Plan: CT chest every 6 months for 2 years, then yearly. Next 01/2024. Copy to PCP.

Thoracic Surgery

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Came in originally for the postponed BP check but says the real reason is a lump on the left testicle he noticed in the shower about 3 weeks ago. Not painful, hasn't grown that he can tell. No trauma, no urinary symptoms, no fever. No back pain, no cough, no breast tenderness.

Exam: Firm, nontender, irregular mass in the lower pole of the left testis, about 2-3 cm, does not transilluminate. Epididymis separate and normal. Right testis normal. No inguinal nodes. No gynecomastia. Abdomen soft. BP fine.

A/P
1. Left testicular mass - solid intratesticular mass in a man is cancer until shown otherwise; unusual at 62 but must be treated that way. Scrotal ultrasound Thursday. Urgent urology referral placed, called their office directly for a slot in the next 1-2 weeks; they will draw tumor markers.
2. HTN - at goal on lisinopril 5.
Discussed honestly with him. He laughed that he 'just finished with the last one'. Will call with the ultrasound.

reports.text:
Indication: Palpable left testicular mass.
Findings: Right testis 4.4 x 2.6 x 2.9 cm, homogeneous, normal flow. Left testis contains a 2.8 cm heterogeneous solid intratesticular mass in the lower pole with internal vascularity. Both epididymides normal. No hydrocele. No varicocele.
reports.conclusion: 2.8 cm solid vascular intratesticular mass, left testis, highly suspicious for testicular neoplasm. Right testis normal.

reports.text:
Specimen: Left testis and spermatic cord, radical orchiectomy.
Gross: Testis 5.2 x 3.4 x 3.1 cm with a 3.0 cm variegated tan-white mass in the lower pole. Spermatic cord 9.5 cm.
Microscopic: Non-seminomatous germ cell tumor. Tumor confined to the testis; tunica vaginalis not involved. Rete testis not involved. Spermatic cord margin negative.
reports.conclusion: Non-seminomatous germ cell tumor, left testis, 3.0 cm, confined to the testis; spermatic cord margin negative.

documents.title: Urology Consultation and Operative Summary
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Patient: Andrew Marino  DOB 03/08/1961

Seen in clinic 12/21/2023 at the request of his primary care physician for a left testicular mass. 62-year-old man, about a month of a painless left testicular lump. Ultrasound 12/14: 2.8 cm solid vascular left intratesticular mass. PMH notable for stage IA lung adenocarcinoma s/p LUL lobectomy 01/2023, hypertension. Former smoker. Allergies: iodinated contrast, sulfonamide antibiotics.
Exam in clinic: firm left lower-pole mass, right testis normal, no adenopathy.
Tumor markers 12/21: AFP 412 ng/mL (elevated).

Plan carried out: left radical inguinal orchiectomy 01/09/2024, outpatient. Uneventful; discharged same day.

Pathology (01/12): non-seminomatous germ cell tumor, 3.0 cm, confined to the testis, cord margin negative.

Assessment: Left testicular NSGCT. Referred to medical oncology for staging and to follow the markers; repeat AFP in 3 weeks.
Meds: lisinopril 5 mg daily, acetaminophen as needed. Post-op: acetaminophen; ice; no heavy lifting for 2 weeks.

Urology

documents.title: Call re orchiectomy pathology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed urology note and path. Called Andrew - he already heard from urology, sounded steadier than I expected. Oncology appointment 2/6. Told him to message anytime. Problem list updated.

events.reason: testicular germ cell tumor, staging and treatment

reports.study: CT chest, abdomen and pelvis without contrast
reports.text:
Indication: Staging, left testicular non-seminomatous germ cell tumor s/p orchiectomy.
Technique: Helical CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis without IV contrast (contrast allergy). Oral contrast given.
Comparison: CT chest 07/11/2023.
Findings: Chest: postsurgical changes of left upper lobectomy. No pulmonary nodules. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. Abdomen and pelvis: no retroperitoneal, pelvic or inguinal adenopathy. Liver, spleen, adrenals and pancreas unremarkable within the limits of a non-contrast study. Kidneys without hydronephrosis. Post-orchiectomy changes in the left inguinal canal. No osseous lesions.
reports.conclusion: No evidence of metastatic disease. Post-lobectomy and post-orchiectomy changes.

documents.title: Medical Oncology Consultation
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
RE: Andrew Marino, 62M
Referring: Urology; copy to primary care

Diagnosis: Left testicular non-seminomatous germ cell tumor, s/p radical orchiectomy 01/09/2024 (3.0 cm, organ-confined, cord margin negative).

History: Painless left testicular mass, AFP 412 before orchiectomy. Also stage IA lung adenocarcinoma resected 01/2023, on CT surveillance. Hypertension. Former smoker, 40 pack-years, quit 08/2022. Kidney function normal.
Meds: lisinopril 5 mg daily; acetaminophen prn.
Allergies: iodinated contrast (hives); sulfonamide antibiotics (rash).

Staging CT C/A/P without contrast 01/29: no adenopathy or metastases.
AFP 01/30 (3 weeks post-op): 188 ng/mL - falling but well above normal and not on the expected half-life curve.

Assessment: Persistently elevated AFP after orchiectomy with no radiographic disease: stage IS. This is treated as disseminated disease; surveillance is not appropriate.

Plan: BEP x 3 cycles, starting 02/12/2024, 21-day cycles. We talked at length about toxicity at his age, including bleomycin lung injury (older age, prior lung surgery and smoking history raise the risk) and cisplatin effects on kidneys and hearing. Will watch symptoms and creatinine each cycle. AFP every cycle.

Medical Oncology

documents.title: Check-in
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Per PCP request called pt between cycles 1 and 2. Tired for a week after each round, some nausea that is manageable, eating OK. No fever. Cycle 2 starts today actually, he is at the infusion center. Reminded him to call oncology first for fever. Nothing needed from us.

documents.title: Oncology Follow-up
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Mr. Marino completed cycle 3 of BEP on 04/15/2024. Fatigue improving, appetite returning, a few pounds down over treatment. No cough or breathlessness today, no tinnitus, no numbness of the feet.
AFP 04/23: 4 ng/mL - normal.
Exam: lungs clear, no edema.
Creatinine has drifted up over the course; he knows to keep drinking fluids. Asked his PCP to recheck kidney function in about 6 weeks.

Assessment: Stage IS NSGCT, marker normalization after 3 cycles of BEP. Complete response.
Plan: Surveillance with markers every 2 months and CT at 6 months (~11/2024, chest without contrast plus MRI abdomen/pelvis given his contrast allergy). Lung cancer CT surveillance can be folded into the same imaging.

Medical Oncology

conditions.label: History of left testicular non-seminomatous germ cell tumor

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every morning

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
First visit since BEP (3 cycles, done 4/15) for left testicular NSGCT. AFP back to normal in April; oncology calls it a complete response, surveillance now.

S: Energy coming back, maybe 75%. Down about 4 kg since winter. Feet fine. Breathing OK on his walks. No urinary symptoms.
Home BP readings 140s-150s/88-92 the last month.
Meds: lisinopril 5 daily, acetaminophen rarely.

O: BP 148/90 (repeat similar). Weight 84 kg. Lungs clear. Heart RRR. No edema.
Labs today (back this afternoon): creatinine 1.8, from 1.15 before chemo; eGFR in the low 40s. UA bland.

A/P
1. CKD stage 3b - after cisplatin; oncology had flagged the rising creatinine. Will repeat in 3 months to see where it settles, but the chemo injury is usually lasting. Avoid NSAIDs, contrast is already off the table, renally dose anything new.
2. HTN - above goal. Not raising lisinopril much with this creatinine; adding furosemide 20 mg each morning. His sulfa antibiotic rash is not a reason to avoid it - cross-reactivity with non-antibiotic sulfonamides is low, explained, he is fine with it. BMP in 2 weeks.
3. Hx testicular NSGCT - surveillance with oncology. Problem list updated.
4. Hx stage I NSCLC - imaging with oncology's in November.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: BMP result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Creatinine stable after starting furosemide, potassium and sodium fine. Pt messaged home BP now 128-134/78-82. Continue.

reports.text:
Comparison: None available at this facility.
Findings: Postsurgical changes of left upper lobectomy with mild left volume loss and surgical clips. Bibasilar reticular opacities. No focal consolidation. No pleural effusion. No pneumothorax. Heart size normal.
reports.conclusion: Bibasilar reticular opacities. Post-lobectomy changes on the left.

orders.reason: cough, exertional dyspnea, bibasilar opacities after bleomycin

documents.title: Office Visit - cough
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Dry cough since about early June, and getting winded with things that were easy in the spring - one flight of stairs, carrying groceries in. No fever, no sputum, no chest pain, no leg swelling, no orthopnea. Not smoking. Finished BEP in April.

O: SpO2 93% at rest on room air. Afebrile. Fine dry crackles at both bases. Heart RRR, no gallop. No JVD, no edema.
CXR in office: bibasilar reticular opacities, post-lobectomy changes on the left, no consolidation or effusion.

A/P
Cough and exertional dyspnea 2-4 months after bleomycin, basal crackles, new bibasilar reticulation, lower resting sat. Bleomycin lung toxicity is the concern. No sign of infection or heart failure on exam.
- Pulmonology referral, marked urgent; message sent to his oncologist as well.
- Reviewed red flags: worsening breathlessness at rest, fever - call same day.
- No new medicines today.

events.reason: cough and exertional dyspnea after bleomycin

medications.sig: 2 liters per minute by nasal cannula, continuous

reports.text:
Indication: Cough and dyspnea after bleomycin. High-resolution protocol.
Technique: Volumetric thin-section CT of the chest without IV contrast, supine and prone, inspiratory and expiratory.
Comparison: CT chest/abdomen/pelvis 01/29/2024.
Findings: New bilateral lower-lobe predominant subpleural reticulation with traction bronchiectasis and superimposed ground-glass opacity. No honeycombing. No air trapping. Postsurgical changes of left upper lobectomy, unchanged. No pulmonary nodules. No pleural effusion. No adenopathy.
reports.conclusion: New bibasilar subpleural fibrotic change with ground-glass, in keeping with bleomycin-related lung injury in this clinical setting. Post-lobectomy changes.

documents.title: Pulmonary Consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Andrew Marino, 63 years old
Referred by: primary care

Reason: nonproductive cough and worsening breathlessness on exertion.

HPI: Mr. Marino started BEP on 02/12/2024 for a left testicular non-seminomatous germ cell tumor (3 cycles, completed 04/15). Since about June he has had a dry cough that will not settle and has become steadily more short of breath with exertion; stairs and yard work now stop him. No fever, sputum or hemoptysis. Known to us from his 2022 bronchoscopy; LUL lobectomy 01/2023 for stage IA adenocarcinoma.

Other history: hypertension; CKD stage 3b after cisplatin. Former smoker, 40 pack-years, quit 08/2022. Social alcohol. Retired construction supervisor.
Family: father lung cancer (died 67), paternal uncle renal cell carcinoma, mother hypertension.
Medications: lisinopril 5 mg daily, furosemide 20 mg daily, acetaminophen 650 mg q6h prn.
Allergies: iodinated contrast - urticaria; sulfonamide antibiotics - rash.

Exam: SpO2 91% on room air at rest. Comfortable at rest, speaks full sentences. Fine dry crackles at both lung bases. No clubbing. Heart regular. No edema.

Studies:
- HRCT chest 08/06 (non-contrast): bibasilar subpleural reticulation with traction bronchiectasis and ground-glass; no honeycombing; post-lobectomy changes.
- Full PFTs 08/13: restrictive pattern. TLC 64% predicted. DLCO 41% predicted.
- 6-minute walk 08/13 on room air: nadir SpO2 86%.

Impression: Bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis.

Plan:
1. Prednisone 10 mg daily. Will reassess symptoms, saturation and PFTs in 3 months.
2. Home oxygen 2 L/min by nasal cannula, continuous. Order sent to a home oxygen supplier; qualifying walk test documented above.
3. Bleomycin must never be given again - please add to his record.
4. Pulmonary rehab information given.
5. Return 3 months.

Pulmonary Medicine

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after pulmonology 8/13. Diagnosis: bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis (HRCT bibasilar fibrosis, restrictive PFTs with TLC 64% and DLCO 41%, walk sat down to 86%). Started prednisone 10 mg daily and oxygen 2 L continuous.

S: Oxygen delivered last week - concentrator at home and portable tanks. Hates the tubing but admits he can do more with it. Cough a little less. On prednisone 13 days, no problems with it so far.
Meds reconciled: lisinopril 5, furosemide 20 qAM, prednisone 10 daily, oxygen 2 L/min NC continuous, acetaminophen prn.
Allergies: contrast, sulfa abx. Added note to chart: no bleomycin, ever.

O: SpO2 95% on 2 L. Fine bibasilar crackles. No edema. BP fine.

A/P
1. Bleomycin pulmonary fibrosis - per pulm. Oxygen certification paperwork signed today for the supplier.
2. Long-term prednisone - added iatrogenic immunosuppression to the problem list so it is visible to anyone treating him for an infection. Glucose on today's BMP. Call early with fever or a cough that changes.
3. CKD 3b - creatinine stable.
4. HTN - at goal on lisinopril + furosemide.
5. Vaccines: flu, COVID and RSV this fall (RSV given his lung disease). Avoid live vaccines on prednisone.
PHQ-9 3. RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Home oxygen paperwork
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Oxygen supplier faxed the certificate of medical necessity and request for the signed face-to-face note. Sent 8/26 visit note and pulm walk test. PCP signed CMN. Faxed back 1:10 pm, confirmation received.

procedures.procedure: Immunization administration

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN

reports.text:

documents.title: RE: kidney
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Andrew, these are fair questions and I'm sorry you're facing another one. Smoking raises the risk of both lung and kidney cancer, and the family history matters too; sometimes there is no single reason. Losing a kidney will lower your kidney function further, and we will plan around that with urology - they weigh it before deciding how much to remove. I want to see you before any surgery. The front desk will book a pre-op visit once urology sets a date.

conditions.label: Metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma

documents.title: Medical Oncology Follow-up
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
RE: Andrew Marino, 64M
cc: primary care, urology, pulmonology

Known to me: testicular NSGCT, stage IS, complete response to BEP x3 (2024), markers normal since. Now clear cell RCC, left radical nephrectomy 01/08/2025 (6.5 cm, ISUP 3, organ-confined, N0). Also stage IA LUL adenocarcinoma resected 2023, bleomycin pulmonary fibrosis on prednisone 10 mg and continuous 2 L O2, CKD 3b.

CT chest 03/24: right lung nodules seen in November have grown (largest 9 to 14 mm) and there are two new ones. AFP normal.

Assessment: With three cancer histories, the source matters. Multiple bilateral-pattern growing nodules appearing around the time of a high-grade clear cell RCC, with normal germ cell markers and a different pattern from his solitary lung primary, are most consistent with metastatic clear cell RCC. The nodules are small and his lungs fibrotic, so I don't think a biopsy is safe right now; if a lesion grows out of pattern we will sample it.
Diagnosis: metastatic clear cell RCC to the lungs.

Treatment: Immune checkpoint combinations are the usual first choice, but with bleomycin lung injury and oxygen dependence the risk of immune pneumonitis is too high in my judgment. Plan sunitinib 50 mg daily, 4 weeks on and 2 weeks off (6-week courses), first course starting 05/05/2025. No dose change needed for his kidney function. Reviewed side effects: fatigue, mouth sores, hand-foot skin changes, diarrhea, blood pressure rise, thyroid effects, low counts. Labs every 2-3 weeks through our office. Restaging CT after 2 courses.

Medical Oncology

documents.title: Oncology Follow-up
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Andrew Marino, 64
Dx: metastatic clear cell RCC (lung), on sunitinib since 05/05/2025. History of bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis, stage IA lung adenocarcinoma s/p LUL lobectomy, testicular NSGCT in remission, CKD 3b.

Interval: Finished his second 6-week course of sunitinib (cycle 2 ended 07/27). Tired during the on-weeks, recovers on the off-weeks. Breathing unchanged on 2 L. Weight stable.
Meds: sunitinib 50 mg 4/2, prednisone 10 mg, lisinopril 5 mg, furosemide 20 mg, O2 2 L continuous, acetaminophen prn.
Allergies: iodinated contrast - urticaria; sulfonamide antibiotics - rash.

Labs today: calcium 10.8 mg/dL; hemoglobin 18 g/dL.
CT chest 08/11: mixed response - most nodules smaller or stable, dominant right lower lobe nodule up to 21 mm.

Assessment: Mixed response after 2 courses. The calcium and hemoglobin are both above normal; in RCC these are classically paraneoplastic and I will follow them rather than act on them now. The enlarging RLL nodule is now large enough to sample, and given his prior lung primary I want tissue before calling this progression of RCC.

Procedure: CT-guided core biopsy of the right lower lobe nodule performed this afternoon by interventional radiology. Post-procedure film without pneumothorax. Discharged home.

Plan: Pathology to follow. Continue sunitinib, course 3 to start 09/01 if biopsy confirms RCC. Recheck calcium and counts with next labs. Encourage fluids.

Medical Oncology

documents.title: Oncology Follow-up
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Andrew Marino, 64, here with his wife.
Dx: metastatic clear cell RCC to lung (biopsy-proven 08/2025) on sunitinib since 05/2025; bleomycin pulmonary fibrosis on 2 L O2 and prednisone 10 mg; stage IA LUL adenocarcinoma s/p lobectomy 2023; testicular NSGCT in remission; CKD 3b.

Interval: Completed his fifth course of sunitinib 01/04. CT chest 01/26: new 3.4 cm spiculated right upper lobe mass, other nodules stable. This could be a new lung primary - he has had one before - or an RCC metastasis behaving differently from the rest.

Today he looks worn out. When I started to lay out options, he said he understands the cancer is serious and that his wife has been reading about newer treatments and wants him to try all of them, then after a pause said he is just exhausted. His wife cut in right away and told him he cannot quit now.

I slowed down. I told them both there is no decision to make today, that being tired is information and not giving up, and that whatever he chooses we keep treating his symptoms. He agreed to a CT-guided biopsy of the RUL mass so we know what we are dealing with. Both agreed to meet with palliative care - framed as an extra layer of support, not an ending.

Plan:
1. Hold sunitinib for now (treatment break while we sort this out).
2. CT-guided biopsy of the RUL mass; IR to schedule. Pulmonology aware given his fibrosis.
3. Palliative care referral sent.
4. See me after the biopsy result, 3/30.
Copy to PCP.

Medical Oncology

documents.title: Outpatient Palliative Care Consultation
documents.author: palliative care
documents.body:
Patient: Andrew Marino, 65
Referred by: medical oncology

Mr. Marino has metastatic clear cell RCC to the lungs, on a sunitinib break since 02/16 with a new right upper lobe mass awaiting biopsy, plus bleomycin pulmonary fibrosis on continuous 2 L oxygen and prednisone 10 mg, a resected stage IA lung adenocarcinoma, a treated testicular germ cell tumor and CKD 3b. Seen with his wife.

Symptoms: fatigue is the biggest burden (6/10), worse in the afternoon. Breathlessness on exertion, at his baseline on 2 L. Pain 0-1/10, acetaminophen occasionally. Appetite reduced. Sleep fair. Mood: worried, not depressed by his account.

Understanding and goals: Knows the cancer is not curable. Wants to know the biopsy result before deciding anything. Values time at home and clear thinking. His wife wants him to keep all options open; they both said they feel heard today. Health care proxy (wife) completed with PCP on 03/03.

Recommendations:
1. Fatigue: pacing, scheduled rest, short walks with oxygen; no new medicine for now.
2. Breathlessness: fan to face, pursed-lip breathing, keep O2 at 2 L.
3. Continue acetaminophen as needed; avoid NSAIDs (single kidney, CKD).
4. Will follow alongside oncology; next visit in about 3 months, sooner if needed.

Palliative Care

documents.body:
Andrew Marino, 65, with his wife.

The right upper lobe biopsy (03/18) shows metastatic clear cell RCC - so not a new lung cancer. This mass grew while he was on sunitinib, which means the RCC is progressing through first-line therapy.

He feels better six weeks off the drug: more energy, eating a little more. Breathing at baseline on 2 L.

Options discussed: (a) second-line oral targeted therapy, with similar side effects to what he had; (b) a treatment break with CT in 3 months and starting therapy if there is meaningful growth or symptoms; (c) focusing on comfort with palliative care. Immunotherapy remains a poor choice for his lungs. Clinical trials: none he is eligible for nearby given his oxygen needs.

He chose (b) today. His wife asked whether waiting would close doors; I told her honestly that a few months of watching in someone feeling this much better is reasonable and that the option of treatment stays open. She accepted it, with tears.

Plan: No systemic therapy for now. CT chest in late June. Return early July. Palliative care continues. Copy to PCP.

Medical Oncology

documents.title: Palliative Care Follow-up
documents.author: palliative care
documents.body:
Andrew Marino, 65. Metastatic clear cell RCC to lung, off systemic therapy since February; bleomycin pulmonary fibrosis on 2 L O2 and prednisone 10 mg; CKD 3b.

Seen 08/06 with his wife. Fatigue unchanged (5-6/10), breathlessness at baseline, pain minimal on occasional acetaminophen. Weight steady. He has not yet decided about restarting treatment and sees oncology later this month. He talked about what a good day looks like for him: coffee on the porch, a visit from family, an afternoon nap without feeling guilty about it.

Recommendations: continue current approach; no medication changes. Revisit MOLST with PCP and oncology once the treatment decision is made. Follow-up in 3 months.

Palliative Care
